lessons.title: Blessings of Allah Almighty
lessons.notes_html:
The Blessings of Allah

  • Allah Almighty has given us many blessings.
  • From air we get breathing, and from water we get drinking, washing and growing crops.
  • The sun gives us heat and light.
  • Plants give us food and growing seeds.
  • Animals give us milk, meat and riding.

Words We Say

  • When a Muslim plans to do something, he says Insha Allah — if Almighty Allah wills.
  • When he sees or hears something good, he says MashaAllah — as Almighty Allah willed.
  • We thank Allah by saying Alhamdulillah.
  • When a Muslim sneezes, the one who hears him says YarhamukAllah — may Allah have mercy on you.
  • We praise Allah by saying SubhanAllah — glory be to Allah, He is free from every fault.

Key Points

  • Air, water, the sun, plants and animals are blessings of Allah.
  • We should thank Almighty Allah for all His blessings.

mcqs.q: What do we get from the air around us?
mcqs.why: Air is a blessing of Allah. We breathe air all the time, and we cannot live without breathing.

mcqs.q: What do animals give us?
mcqs.why: From animals we get milk and meat, and some animals are used for riding, as the matching activity tells us.

mcqs.q: What does the sun give us?
mcqs.why: The sun is a blessing of Allah which gives us heat and light every day.

mcqs.q: What do we get from water?
mcqs.why: We use water for drinking and washing, and water also helps us to grow crops.

mcqs.q: What do plants give us?
mcqs.why: Plants give us food to eat, and from plants we also get seeds to grow more plants.

mcqs.q: When a Muslim plans to do something, what does he say?
mcqs.why: When a Muslim plans to do something, he says Insha Allah, which means: if Almighty Allah wills.

mcqs.q: When a Muslim sees or hears something good, he says ______.
mcqs.why: On seeing or hearing something good, a Muslim says MashaAllah, which means: as Almighty Allah willed.

mcqs.q: Muslims thank Allah by saying ______.
mcqs.why: We should thank Almighty Allah for every blessing He gives us, and we thank Him by saying Alhamdulillah.

mcqs.q: When a Muslim sneezes, the one who hears him says ______.
mcqs.why: YarhamukAllah means: may Almighty Allah have mercy on you. The one who sneezes himself says Alhamdulillah.

mcqs.q: Muslims praise Allah by saying ______.
mcqs.why: SubhanAllah means: glory be to Almighty Allah; He is free from every fault.

lessons.title: Fasting
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Fasting?

  • Fasting means to give up eating and drinking for Almighty Allah.
  • Fasting is a time of prayer and of doing good deeds to help the poor and needy.
  • Through fasting we learn patience, we understand the feelings of those who do not get enough food, and we learn to help others.

Fasting in Different Religions

  • Muslims fast in the month of Ramazan, from sunrise to sunset.
  • Christians fast in Lent.
  • Hindus fast during their religious festivals, such as Maha Shivaratri and just before Diwali.

Sehri, Iftari and Taraveeh

  • Muslims begin their fast by eating Sehri before sunrise.
  • They end their fast by eating Iftari at sunset.
  • The special prayer offered during Ramazan is called Taraveeh, and Muslims also recite the Holy Quran in this month.

Key Points

  • Fasting means giving up eating and drinking for Allah.
  • Muslims fast in Ramazan from sunrise to sunset.
  • Sehri is eaten before sunrise and Iftari at sunset.

mcqs.q: What does fasting mean?
options: To eat a lot of food
To give up eating and drinking for Almighty Allah
mcqs.why: Fasting means to give up eating and drinking for Almighty Allah. It is also a time of prayer and good deeds.

mcqs.q: Muslims fast in the month of ______.
mcqs.why: Muslims fast in the month of Ramazan. They fast from sunrise to sunset in this holy month.

mcqs.q: A fast is kept from ______.
mcqs.why: The fast begins before sunrise with Sehri and ends at sunset with Iftari, so it lasts from sunrise to sunset.

mcqs.q: Christians fast in ______.
mcqs.why: Christians fast in Lent. This is their special time of fasting in the year.

mcqs.q: Hindus fast ______.
mcqs.why: Hindus fast during their religious festivals such as Maha Shivaratri and just before Diwali.

mcqs.q: Muslims begin their fast by eating ______.
mcqs.why: Sehri is eaten before sunrise, and then the fast is kept for the whole day.

mcqs.q: Sehri is eaten ______.
mcqs.why: Sehri is the meal eaten before sunrise, before the fast of the day begins.

mcqs.q: Muslims end their fast by eating ______.
mcqs.why: Iftari is eaten at sunset and the family breaks the fast together.

mcqs.q: The special prayer offered by Muslims during Ramazan is called ______.
mcqs.why: The special prayer offered during Ramazan is called Taraveeh. Muslims also recite the Holy Quran in Ramazan.

mcqs.q: Through fasting we learn ______.
options: Patience and helping the poor and needy
mcqs.why: Through fasting we learn patience, we understand the feelings of hungry people, and we learn to do good deeds.

lessons.title: Religious Festivals
lessons.notes_html:
This is an activity lesson: you write sentences to describe how you celebrate a religious festival. The model answer in the book describes Eid-ul-Fitr.

How We Celebrate Eid-ul-Fitr

  • Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawal after the fasting month of Ramazan.
  • We prepare for Eid by decorating our home, and we make new clothes and buy new shoes.
  • We give Fitra to the poor and needy so that they can also enjoy Eid.
  • On Eid day we wear new clothes and go to the mosque or Eidgah for Eid prayers.
  • After the prayers we wish each other Eid Mubarak, children receive Eidi, and we eat delicious food and sweets with our family and friends.

Key Points

  • Eid-ul-Fitr comes after Ramazan, on the first day of Shawal.
  • We give Fitra to the poor so that they can also enjoy Eid.
  • On Eid we wear new clothes, offer prayers and meet family and friends.

mcqs.q: Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated after the month of ______.
mcqs.why: Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawal, after the fasting month of Ramazan ends.

mcqs.q: Eid-ul-Fitr falls on the first day of ______.
mcqs.why: After the month of Ramazan, the month of Shawal begins, and its first day is Eid-ul-Fitr.

mcqs.q: Before Eid, we give ______ to the poor so that they can also enjoy Eid.
mcqs.why: We give Fitra to the poor and needy before Eid so that they can also enjoy the festival.

mcqs.q: On Eid day, people go for Eid prayers to ______.
mcqs.why: On Eid day we wear new clothes and go to the mosque or Eidgah for Eid prayers.

mcqs.q: After the Eid prayers, people wish each other ______.
mcqs.why: After the prayers we wish each other Eid Mubarak and meet our family and friends happily.

mcqs.q: On Eid, children receive ______.
mcqs.why: Children receive Eidi on Eid, and we eat delicious food and sweets with family and friends.

mcqs.q: How do we prepare for Eid?
options: We decorate our home and make new clothes
mcqs.why: We prepare for Eid by decorating our home, and we make new clothes and buy new shoes.

mcqs.q: What do we eat on Eid?
mcqs.why: On Eid we eat delicious food and sweets with our family and friends after the prayers.

mcqs.q: Why do we give Fitra to the poor?
options: So that they fast for us
So that they give us Eidi
So that they can also enjoy Eid
So that they decorate our home
mcqs.why: Fitra is given to the poor and needy so that they can also buy things and enjoy Eid like us.

mcqs.q: We celebrate Eid with ______.
mcqs.why: Eid is a happy festival which we celebrate together with our family and friends.

lessons.title: End of Unit 1 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
The Blessings of Allah

  • The blessings Almighty Allah has given me are: food, water, air, home, family, sunlight and its warmth, plants and animals.
  • We have to thank Almighty Allah for all these blessings.

Festivals of Different Religions

  • Easter and Christmas are celebrated by Christians. Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus (AS).
  • At the end of Ramazan, Muslims celebrate Eid-ul-Fitr. The special sweet dish of Eid-ul-Fitr is Sheer Khurma.
  • Eid-ul-Azha is celebrated on the 10th day of Zil Hajj. It is also called the Feast of Sacrifice.
  • On Eid-ul-Azha, Muslims sacrifice goats, cows, sheep or camels to recall the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), and the meat is shared among the poor, friends and relatives.
  • Hindus celebrate Holi and Diwali, the festival of lights, when they light small oil lamps called diyas.
  • Jews celebrate Hanukkah and Passover.

Cultural Festivals

  • The Urs of Hazrat Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai is celebrated every year at Bhit Shah for three days, in memory of the great Sufi poet of Sindh.
  • Other cultural festivals are Sindhi Culture Day (Topi Ajrak Day) and the Mango Festival.

Key Points

  • People of every religion celebrate their religious festivals every year.
  • Eid-ul-Azha is the Feast of Sacrifice, on the 10th of Zil Hajj.
  • Diwali is the festival of lights, celebrated by Hindus.

mcqs.q: Easter is celebrated by ______.
mcqs.why: Christians celebrate Christmas and Easter. Easter is a religious festival of the Christians.

mcqs.q: At the end of the fasting month of Ramazan, Muslims celebrate ______.
mcqs.why: Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawal, at the end of the fasting month of Ramazan.

mcqs.q: Eid-ul-Azha is celebrated on the 10th day of the Islamic month of ______.
mcqs.why: Eid-ul-Azha is celebrated on the 10th day of Zil Hajj. It is also called the Feast of Sacrifice.

mcqs.q: Eid-ul-Azha is also called the ______.
mcqs.why: On Eid-ul-Azha Muslims sacrifice animals, so this Eid is also called the Feast of Sacrifice.

mcqs.q: Jews celebrate ______.
mcqs.why: Jews celebrate Hanukkah and Passover. People of every religion celebrate their festivals every year.

mcqs.q: On Eid-ul-Azha, Muslims sacrifice animals to recall the sacrifice of ______.
mcqs.why: Muslims sacrifice animals on Eid-ul-Azha to recall the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) for Allah.

mcqs.q: The special sweet dish eaten on Eid-ul-Fitr is ______.
mcqs.why: Sheer Khurma, a sweet vermicelli dish, is eaten and served to guests on Eid-ul-Fitr.

mcqs.q: Christmas celebrates the birth of ______.
mcqs.why: Christmas is the religious festival to celebrate the birth of Jesus (AS), and it is celebrated by Christians.

mcqs.q: Diwali is known as the festival of ______.
mcqs.why: Diwali is the festival of lights. On Diwali, Hindus light small oil lamps called diyas.

mcqs.q: The Urs of Hazrat Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai is celebrated at ______.
mcqs.why: The Urs is celebrated every year at Bhit Shah for three days, in memory of the great Sufi poet of Sindh.

lessons.title: Our Country Pakistan
lessons.notes_html:
This is a map activity lesson: you join the dots to make the map of Pakistan and write the names of the provinces and their capital cities.

Provinces of Pakistan

  • Pakistan has four provinces.
  • Sindh — capital: Karachi.
  • Punjab — capital: Lahore.
  • Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) — capital: Peshawar.
  • Balochistan — capital: Quetta.

Our Capital

  • The capital of Pakistan is Islamabad.
  • Gilgit Baltistan is also a part of Pakistan.

Key Points

  • Pakistan has four provinces: Sindh, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.
  • Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan.

mcqs.q: How many provinces does Pakistan have?
mcqs.why: Pakistan has four provinces: Sindh, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

mcqs.q: The capital of Pakistan is ______.
mcqs.why: Islamabad is the capital of the whole country, Pakistan. Karachi, Lahore and Quetta are provincial capitals.

mcqs.q: Karachi is the capital of ______.
mcqs.why: Karachi is the capital city of the province of Sindh, as the map activity in this lesson tells us.

mcqs.q: Lahore is the capital of ______.
mcqs.why: Lahore is the capital city of Punjab, the biggest province of Pakistan by population.

mcqs.q: Peshawar is the capital of ______.
mcqs.why: Peshawar is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which is also written in short as KPK.

mcqs.q: Quetta is the capital of ______.
mcqs.why: Quetta is the capital city of Balochistan, one of the four provinces of Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a province of Pakistan?
mcqs.why: Sindh is one of the four provinces of Pakistan. Delhi, Dhaka and Kabul are cities of other countries.

mcqs.q: Gilgit Baltistan is ______.
mcqs.why: Gilgit Baltistan is also a part of Pakistan, along with the four provinces.

mcqs.q: The four provinces of Pakistan are Sindh, Punjab, Balochistan and ______.
mcqs.why: The four provinces are Sindh, Punjab, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK).

mcqs.q: The map activity in this lesson shows ______.
options: The map of Pakistan with its provinces
mcqs.why: In this activity we join the dots to make the map of Pakistan and write the provinces and their capitals.

lessons.title: Our Flag
lessons.notes_html:
The first activity of this lesson is drawing and colouring: you draw the flag of Pakistan and colour it. Here the flag is described in words.

The Flag of Pakistan

  • The colours of the flag of Pakistan are green and white.
  • The green colour shows prosperity and the Muslim majority.
  • The white colour shows peace and the minority.
  • The crescent on the flag shows progress.
  • The star on the flag shows light and knowledge.

Flags of Our Neighbours

  • China — colour: red — symbol: yellow stars, one big star and four small stars.
  • India — colours: saffron, white and green — symbol: a blue wheel (Ashoka Chakra) in the centre.
  • Iran — colours: green, white and red — symbol: a red national emblem in the centre.
  • Afghanistan — colours: black, red and green — symbol: the national emblem in the centre.

Key Points

  • Our flag is green and white, with a crescent and a star.
  • The crescent shows progress and the star shows light and knowledge.

mcqs.q: The colours of the flag of Pakistan are ______.
mcqs.why: The colours of the flag of Pakistan are green and white, with a white crescent and star.

mcqs.q: The green colour of our flag shows ______.
mcqs.why: The green colour shows prosperity and the Muslim majority of Pakistan.

mcqs.q: The white colour of our flag shows ______.
mcqs.why: The white colour shows peace and the minority, who also live in Pakistan with full rights.

mcqs.q: The crescent on the flag shows ______.
mcqs.why: The crescent on the flag of Pakistan is a symbol of progress.

mcqs.q: The star on the flag shows ______.
mcqs.why: The star on the flag shows light and knowledge, and it is drawn together with the crescent.

mcqs.q: The flag of China is ______ in colour, with yellow stars.
mcqs.why: China's flag is red, and its symbol is yellow stars — one big star and four small stars.

mcqs.q: The flag of India has a blue ______ in the centre.
mcqs.why: India's flag has saffron, white and green colours, with a blue wheel, the Ashoka Chakra, in the centre.

mcqs.q: The colours of the flag of Iran are ______.
mcqs.why: Iran's flag has green, white and red colours, with a red national emblem in the centre.

mcqs.q: The flag of Afghanistan has ______ in the centre.
mcqs.why: Afghanistan's flag has black, red and green colours, with the national emblem in the centre.

mcqs.q: How many stars are there on the flag of China?
options: Five — one big star and four small stars
mcqs.why: China's flag has five yellow stars: one big star and four small stars on the red flag.

lessons.title: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah
lessons.notes_html:
This is an activity lesson: you make a fact file on Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah by completing the sentences.

Fact File

  • Name: Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah.
  • Date of birth: 25th December, 1876.
  • Place of birth: Karachi.
  • Profession: lawyer.
  • Achievements: he led the struggle for Pakistan and made Pakistan; he was the first Governor General of Pakistan.
  • Date of death: 11th September, 1948.
  • Buried at: Karachi (Mazar-e-Quaid).

Key Points

  • Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah is the founder of Pakistan.
  • He was born in Karachi in 1876 and was a lawyer by profession.
  • He was the first Governor General of Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah was born on ______.
mcqs.why: Quaid-i-Azam was born on 25th December 1876 in Karachi, as his fact file tells us.

mcqs.q: Quaid-i-Azam was born in ______.
mcqs.why: The place of birth of Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah is Karachi.

mcqs.q: The profession of Quaid-i-Azam was ______.
mcqs.why: Quaid-i-Azam was a lawyer by profession before he led the struggle for Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Quaid-i-Azam led the struggle for ______.
mcqs.why: He led the struggle for Pakistan and made Pakistan, which is his great achievement.

mcqs.q: Quaid-i-Azam was the first ______ of Pakistan.
mcqs.why: Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah was the first Governor General of Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Quaid-i-Azam died on ______.
mcqs.why: Quaid-i-Azam died on 11th September 1948, about one year after Pakistan was made.

mcqs.q: Quaid-i-Azam is buried in ______.
mcqs.why: He is buried in Karachi, and his tomb is called Mazar-e-Quaid.

mcqs.q: The founder of Pakistan is ______.
mcqs.why: Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah is the founder of Pakistan; he worked very hard to make Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an achievement of Quaid-i-Azam?
mcqs.why: His achievements are that he led the struggle for Pakistan, made Pakistan, and became its first Governor General.

mcqs.q: Quaid-i-Azam was born in the year ______.
mcqs.why: Quaid-i-Azam was born in the year 1876, on the 25th of December, in Karachi.

lessons.title: Government
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Government?

  • A group of elected people who look after everything for the country is called the government.
  • Just as a mother and father take care of the family, the government takes care of the whole country and its people.

Responsibilities of a Government

  • To provide people their basic needs, like education and health care.
  • To ensure the supply of clean water, gas and electricity.
  • To build roads, railway stations and airports, and to keep the life and property of people safe.

Our Responsibilities

  • Going to school and studying hard.
  • Keeping our home, school, locality and park clean.
  • Obeying the traffic rules.

Key Points

  • The government looks after the whole country and its people.
  • We also have responsibilities towards our country.

mcqs.q: A government is ______.
options: A group of elected people who look after the country
mcqs.why: A group of elected people who look after everything for the country is called the government.

mcqs.q: The government takes care of ______.
options: The whole country and its people
mcqs.why: Just as parents take care of the family, the government takes care of the whole country and its people.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a responsibility of the government?
options: To provide education and health care
mcqs.why: The government provides people their basic needs, like education and health care.

mcqs.q: The government ensures the supply of ______.
mcqs.why: It is the government's responsibility to ensure the supply of clean water, gas and electricity to the people.

mcqs.q: The government builds ______.
mcqs.why: The government builds roads, railway stations and airports, and keeps the life and property of people safe.

mcqs.q: The government keeps people's ______ safe.
mcqs.why: Keeping the life and property of the people safe is an important responsibility of the government.

mcqs.q: Which of these is OUR responsibility towards our country?
options: To go to school and study hard
mcqs.why: Our responsibilities are to study hard, keep places clean and obey the traffic rules.

mcqs.q: We should keep ______ clean.
options: Our home, school, locality and park
mcqs.why: Keeping our home, school, locality and park clean is our responsibility towards our country.

mcqs.q: On the road, we should ______.
mcqs.why: Obeying the traffic rules is one of our responsibilities towards our country and keeps us safe.

mcqs.q: Just as parents care for the family, the government cares for ______.
mcqs.why: The government takes care of the whole country and its people, just as a mother and father take care of the family.

lessons.title: End of Unit 2 Exercise

Our Flag Again

Our Country

  • The capital of Pakistan is Islamabad, and the national language is Urdu.

mcqs.q: Pakistan came into being on ______.

mcqs.q: The national language of Pakistan is ______.

mcqs.q: The language spoken in Sindh is ______.
mcqs.why: Sindh's capital is Karachi and the language spoken in Sindh is Sindhi.

mcqs.why: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's capital is Peshawar and the language spoken there is Pashto.

mcqs.why: Balochistan's capital is Quetta and the language spoken there is Balochi.

mcqs.q: The flag of Japan has ______ in the centre.
mcqs.why: Japan's flag is white in colour, with a red circle, the sun, in the centre.

mcqs.q: The flag of Saudi Arabia is green with ______.
options: The Kalima written on it and a sword
mcqs.why: Saudi Arabia's flag is green, and its symbol is white Arabic writing, the Kalima, and a sword.

mcqs.q: The flag of Sri Lanka has a ______ holding a sword.
mcqs.why: Sri Lanka's flag has maroon, gold, green and orange colours, and its symbol is a lion holding a sword.

options: Crosses in blue, white and red

lessons.title: Village Life
lessons.notes_html:
This is an activity lesson: you complete the sentences about a day in the life of a woman and a man in a village.

A Day in a Village

  • A village woman and a village man get up at 5 o’clock.
  • For breakfast they eat bread (roti) and tea.
  • In the morning the woman does the housework, feeds the animals and milks them; the man goes to the fields and ploughs the land or takes care of the crop.
  • They eat lunch at 1 o’clock.
  • In the evening the woman cooks the evening meal and takes care of the children; the man returns home and spends time with his family.
  • They go to bed at 9 o’clock.

Why Villagers Go to the Town

  • To get their tools and machines fixed.
  • To get their children taught at school.
  • To get treatment from a doctor when they are sick.
  • To buy things of daily need from the market, and to sell their crops and animals.

Key Points

  • Village people get up early and work hard all day.
  • Villagers go to the town for repairs, school, a doctor, shopping and selling.

mcqs.q: A village woman gets up at ______.
mcqs.why: In a village, both the woman and the man get up early, at 5 o'clock in the morning.

mcqs.q: For breakfast, village people eat ______.
mcqs.why: The village woman and man have bread (roti) and tea for breakfast before starting their work.

mcqs.q: In the morning, a village woman ______.
options: Does the housework, feeds the animals and milks them
mcqs.why: In the morning she does the housework, feeds the animals and milks them.

mcqs.q: Village people eat lunch at ______.
mcqs.why: Both the village woman and the village man eat lunch at 1 o'clock.

mcqs.q: In the morning, a village man goes to ______.
options: The fields to plough the land
mcqs.why: In the morning the village man goes to the fields and ploughs the land or takes care of the crop.

mcqs.q: Village people go to bed at ______.
mcqs.why: After a full day of hard work, village people go to bed at 9 o'clock.

mcqs.q: Villagers go to the town to ______.
options: Get their tools and machines fixed
mcqs.why: Villagers go to the town to get their tools and machines fixed, among other needs.

mcqs.q: When a villager is sick, he goes to the town for ______.
mcqs.why: Villagers go to the town to get treatment from a doctor when they are sick.

mcqs.q: Villagers sell in the town ______.
mcqs.why: Villagers go to the town to sell their crops and animals in the market.

mcqs.q: The children of a village go to the town to ______.
mcqs.why: Villagers take their children to the town to get them taught at school.

lessons.title: Changes in the Village Over Time
lessons.notes_html:
The Village School: Past and Now

  • In the past, the village school was a small one-room building in the town, and the children had to walk very far to get to school.
  • Now there is a two-room primary school in the village, and for secondary school the children go by van to the town.

Transport: Past and Now

  • In the past people travelled on foot, by bicycle, bullock cart and camel cart, and travelling took a long time.
  • Now people use motorcycles, rickshaws, vans, buses and tractor trolleys, so travelling has become fast and easy.

Farm Work: Past and Now

  • Ploughing: with oxen in the past — with a tractor now.
  • Planting: sowing seeds by hand — with machines now.
  • Watering: with a Persian wheel (rahat) and by hand — with tube-well and canal water now.
  • Harvesting: by hand — with a thresher machine now.
  • Taking farm products to market: by bullock cart and camel cart — by truck and tractor trolley now.

Key Points

  • Village life is changing with time: schools, transport and farm work are all better now.
  • Machines have made farm work and travelling fast and easy.

mcqs.q: In the past, the village school was ______.
options: A big college in the village
A two-room school in the village
A small one-room building in the town
mcqs.why: In the past the village school was a small one-room building in the town next to the village.

mcqs.q: Now the village has ______.
options: A one-room school in the town
mcqs.why: Now there is a two-room primary school in the village and most of the children go to this school.

mcqs.q: Children go to the secondary school in the town by ______.
mcqs.why: When children pass primary school, they go by van to a secondary school in the town.

mcqs.q: In the past, people mostly travelled by ______.

lessons.title: City Life
lessons.notes_html:
Facilities in a City

  • Cities have schools, colleges and universities; hospitals and dispensaries; gardens (parks) and playgrounds; bazaars and shopping centres; offices and factories; and big and small roads with public transport.
  • These facilities are provided so that every person can get education, treatment, play, shopping and work.
  • The government alone cannot give a school and a hospital to every person, so private institutions and people also open schools and hospitals.

Village and City

  • People: few in a village, very many in a city.
  • Houses: few and far apart in a village; many and close together in a city.
  • Work: most people are farmers in a village; in a city people work in offices, factories, shops and hospitals.
  • Travel: on foot, bicycle and bullock cart in a village; cars, buses, rickshaws and motorcycles in a city.
  • Environment: a village is quiet and clean; a city has crowds, noise and many vehicles.

Key Points

  • Cities have many facilities for education, health, play, shopping and work.
  • A village is quiet and clean, while a city is crowded and noisy.

lessons.title: The Work People Do
lessons.notes_html:
Workers and Their Work

  • Farmer: grows crops in the land — he provides food for all of us.
  • Teacher: teaches children to read and write — with education children become good citizens.
  • Mason (builder): builds houses and buildings, which we need to live and work in.
  • Policeman: protects people’s lives and property and controls the traffic — his work keeps peace and order.
  • Tailor: stitches clothes, which we all need to wear.
  • Doctor: treats sick people and makes them healthy.
  • Sweeper: cleans the streets and houses — cleanliness keeps diseases away.
  • Factory worker: makes things in a factory, which we use in daily life.
  • Shopkeeper: sells things of daily need at his shop, near our home.
  • Bus driver: drives a bus and takes people to school, work and the shops.

Guess Who I Am

  • Sewing clothes — a tailor. Repairing shoes — a cobbler. Singing a song — a singer. Selling vegetables — a vegetable seller. Selling milk — a milkman (gwala). Selling meat — a butcher.

Key Points

  • Every work helps others, so we should respect every profession.

lessons.title: Caring for One Another
lessons.notes_html:
This is an activity lesson: you think and write about the ways you can help children who have less than you, and how you feel when someone helps you.

How We Can Help

  • I can give them my extra clothes and toys.
  • I can share my food and lunch with them.
  • In studies I can help them by giving my notebooks, books and pencils.
  • In sickness or trouble I can look after them and tell the elders so that they get help.

How We Feel When We Are Helped

  • When I am in need and someone helps me, I feel very happy and peaceful.
  • I feel that I am not alone and that people love me.
  • That is why I should also help others, so that they feel happy in the same way.

Key Points

  • Caring for one another means helping others in their need.

Work of Farmers

Helping at Home and in Class

Village and City: Same and Different

Professions

lessons.title: We Are Born Equal in Honour and Dignity
lessons.notes_html:
Alike and Different

  • We are like the children of our neighbourhood: we all study in the same school and like to play, and we have all been taught to respect our parents and teachers.
  • We are different from each other: our clothes and foods are different, some children speak different languages, and our games and hobbies are also different.
  • In spite of the differences, we are all equal in dignity and respect.

The Story of Sajida

  • Sajida did not respect others. At hand-washing time she would push through the queue and come before everyone else.
  • At lunch time she would eat her own burger first and then eat her classmates’ burgers too, so her friends became annoyed with her.
  • The things of respecting are: waiting for your own turn, not pushing in a queue, not taking others’ things without permission, and caring for others’ feelings.

Meaning of Dignity and Respect

  • Dignity and respect means giving importance to every person, behaving well with him, and not hurting his feelings — just as we want for ourselves.
  • When we respect others, we also get respect.

Key Points

  • All children are equal in dignity and respect, even when they are different.
  • Waiting for our turn and asking permission are ways of respecting others.

lessons.title: Our Rights and Our Responsibilities
lessons.notes_html:
Needs and Wishes

  • Needs are things which are required for a healthy and happy life: bread, clothes, a house, clean water and education.
  • Wishes are things which are not necessary but we want them: new toys, ice cream and a bicycle.
  • If the needs are not fulfilled, the child will become sick, weak and sad, and he will not be able to grow properly.

Rights of Children

  • Children’s rights are those things which every child should get to live a healthy and happy life.
  • Five rights: (1) the right to live, (2) the right to get education, (3) the right to health protection (treatment), (4) the right to bread, clothes and a safe place to live, (5) the right to play and rest.
  • Children’s rights are provided and protected by their elders — parents, teachers and the government.

Responsibilities with Rights

  • Right to live with family — respect parents, help in cleaning the house, love brothers and sisters.
  • Right to play — put the toys away after playing, do not pluck flowers in the park, share toys with friends.
  • Right to health — wash hands before eating, eat vegetables and fruits, do homework daily.
  • Right to bread and clothes — do not waste food, keep clothes clean, be thankful for food.

Key Points

  • Needs are necessary for life; wishes are only things we want.
  • With every right, we also have responsibilities.

lessons.title: Forgiving Others
lessons.notes_html:
This is an activity lesson with a story: you think of a time when a friend hurt you, and you read the story of Sara and Anam.

When a Friend Hurts Us

  • One day my friend took my pencil without asking and did not return it.
  • Instead of fighting, I told the teacher and then talked to my friend with love.
  • At first I felt hurt and angry, but when he said sorry, I felt good.
  • If it happens again, I will first explain with love and forgive him, because by forgiving, friendship stays alive.

The Story of Sara and Anam

  • When Sara saw Anam playing with another girl, Sara felt very angry and sad, because Anam was her best friend.
  • At home Sara remembered the things they had done together: playing house-house, hide and seek and cricket.
  • In the evening Sara went to Anam’s home; both said sorry to each other, hugged each other and became friends again.
  • Sara’s right work was that she herself went and said sorry and saved the friendship.

Key Points

  • Saying sorry and forgiving are both good works.
  • By forgiving, friendship stays alive.

lessons.title: End of Unit 4 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
The Park I Want

  • In my favourite park there will be a big green ground with swings, a slide and a see-saw, trees with benches in their shade, a clean path, a tap of clean water and a dustbin, so every child can play safely.

The Respectful and Forgiving Thing to Do

  • When two children want the same doll or game, ask for a turn, or make a rule at the start that each one will play for a fixed time.
  • If you need a friend’s red pencil, ask for permission first. Taking a thing without asking is against respect.
  • Sonia should pick up her toys when the teacher says so — obeying the teacher is respect.
  • A borrowed bicycle made dirty should be washed well before returning it.
  • Noreen should wait for her turn to tell her story.
  • If Aamir knocks down Bilal’s tower, the forgiving way is: Aamir says sorry and helps Bilal rebuild the tower.

How the Government Gives Us Rights

  • Right to a name and nationality — the government makes the child’s birth certificate and identity card.
  • Right to education — the government builds government schools and gives free books.
  • Right to health — the government builds hospitals and gives free injections (vaccines).
  • Right to play — the government makes parks and playgrounds.

The Poem about Forgiving

  • The poem tells us that as long as we are alive, we should always remember to forgive; we need to forgive and forget, and in return we will get a precious reward.

Key Points

  • Asking for a turn and asking permission are respectful habits.
  • The government protects our rights through schools, hospitals and parks.

lessons.title: Our Earth, Our Environment
lessons.notes_html:
Living and Non-Living Things

  • Animals are living things. A table and a chair are non-living things.
  • Living things eat food; non-living things have no life.
  • If a plant does not get air, it will become dead. Plants need air, water and light to stay alive.
  • A football cannot move by itself — only living things can move by themselves.
  • A mango tree cannot save itself from fire, because it cannot run away from fire.

Natural and Man-Made Things

  • Natural things are made by Allah Almighty: a monkey on a tree branch, a forest, a dolphin in the sea.
  • Man-made things are made by people: a cage, a house built in a garden, a goldfish in a glass bowl, a TV in a room.

Key Points

  • Living things eat food and can move by themselves; non-living things have no life.
  • Natural things are made by Allah; man-made things are made by people.

lessons.title: Natural Resources
lessons.notes_html:
What Are Natural Resources?

  • Natural resources are those things which we get from the natural environment and which are used for our needs.

The Four Natural Resources

  • (1) Land — from land we get food and minerals.
  • (2) Water — water is needed for drinking.
  • (3) Plants — from plants we get food and wood.
  • (4) Animals — from animals we get milk and meat.

Why We Need Them

  • We need natural resources because without them we cannot live.
  • In the coming units we will learn about each of them in detail.

Key Points

  • The four big natural resources are land, water, plants and animals.
  • Natural resources are used for our needs, and we cannot live without them.

mcqs.why: From animals we get milk and meat. Animals are one of the four natural resources told in the book.

mcqs.q: Without natural resources, we ______.
mcqs.why: We need natural resources because without them we cannot live.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a natural resource?
mcqs.why: Water, plants and animals are natural resources. A plastic bottle is made by people in a factory.

mcqs.q: Natural resources are used for ______.
mcqs.why: Natural resources are things from nature which are used for our needs in daily life.

lessons.title: End of Unit 5 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
A Tree Is a Natural Resource

  • A tree has green leaves, a brown trunk and fruits. From a tree we get fruits, wood and shade.
  • Trees also keep the air clean, so we should plant more trees.

Myself and My Toy

  • I can eat food, talk and walk by myself; my toy cannot do these things.
  • That is why I am a living thing and my toy is a non-living thing.

Natural Resources in Pictures

  • In the pictures of zebras in a plain and birds over water, the natural resources are: the sun (sunlight and heat), water, animals and grass/plants.

How We Use Them

  • Air: we breathe in air; without it we cannot live.
  • Water: we drink it and use it for cooking, washing and watering crops.
  • Plants: we get food (grains, vegetables, fruits), wood and medicines.
  • Animals: we get milk, meat, eggs and skin (leather); some animals are used for riding and carrying loads.

Key Points

  • Air, water, plants and animals are natural resources, and we use each one every day.
  • We should take care of the plants and animals of our environment.

mcqs.q: A tree gives us ______.
mcqs.why: A tree is a natural resource: from it we get fruits, wood and shade, and trees keep the air clean.

mcqs.q: Trees keep the air ______.
mcqs.why: Trees keep the air clean, so we should plant more trees.

mcqs.q: I am a ______ thing; my toy is a ______ thing.
mcqs.why: I can eat, talk and walk by myself; my toy cannot. That is why I am a living thing and my toy is a non-living thing.

mcqs.q: In the pictures of zebras and birds, one natural resource is ______.
mcqs.why: The natural resources in the pictures are the sun (sunlight and heat), water, animals and grass/plants.

mcqs.why: Air is a natural resource: we breathe in air, and without it we cannot live.

mcqs.q: Plants give us food, wood and ______.
mcqs.why: From plants we get food (grains, vegetables, fruits), wood and medicines.

mcqs.q: The skin of animals is used as ______.
mcqs.why: From animals we get milk, meat, eggs and skin, which is used as leather.

mcqs.q: Some animals are used for ______.
mcqs.why: Some animals are used for riding and carrying loads, besides giving us milk, meat and eggs.

mcqs.q: Which of these animals is found in our area?
mcqs.why: The animals found in our area include the dog, goat, pigeon, buffalo and sparrow.

mcqs.q: We should take care of plants and animals because ______.
options: They are part of our environment
mcqs.why: These plants and animals are part of our environment and we should take care of them.

lessons.title: The Earth (Land)
lessons.notes_html:
This is a matching activity lesson: you look at each natural resource and tell what can be made from it.

What We Make from Land Resources

  • Gold — gold jewellery is made from it.
  • Clay — clay pots, like pitchers and bowls, are made from it.
  • Trees — a wooden house is made from their wood.
  • Sheep — wool comes from a sheep, and warm clothes are made from wool.
  • Cotton — thread is made from cotton, and then clothes are made from the thread.

Key Points

  • From the natural resources found in the land, we make many useful things.
  • Gold, clay, trees, sheep and cotton all give us useful materials.

mcqs.q: Gold is used to make ______.
mcqs.why: Gold is a natural resource of the land, and gold jewellery is made from it, as the book's example shows.

mcqs.q: Clay is used to make ______.
mcqs.why: From a pile of clay we make clay pots, such as pitchers and bowls.

mcqs.q: Trees give us wood to make ______.
mcqs.why: Trees are a land resource; from their wood a wooden house is made.

mcqs.q: From a sheep we get ______.
mcqs.why: A sheep gives us wool, and warm clothes are made from sheep's wool.

mcqs.q: Warm clothes are made from ______.
mcqs.why: Balls of wool come from a sheep, and warm clothes are made from sheep's wool.

mcqs.q: Cotton is used to make ______.
mcqs.why: Thread and then clothes are made from cotton, which grows in the land.

mcqs.q: Which of these comes from the land?
mcqs.why: Gold is found in the land. It is one of the natural resources of the land, like clay and cotton.

mcqs.q: Things made from land resources are ______ for us.
mcqs.why: From the natural resources found in the land we make many useful things for our daily life.

mcqs.q: From trees we get ______ for building houses.
mcqs.why: Trees give us wood, and a wooden house is made from the wood of trees.

mcqs.q: Gold, clay, cotton and wool are all ______.
mcqs.why: All these things are found in the land and are its natural resources, from which we make useful things.

lessons.title: Plains
lessons.notes_html:
This is an activity lesson: you tell or describe three uses of plains.

Uses of Plains

  • (1) For building houses to live in, schools, hospitals and offices — buildings are made easily in plain areas.
  • (2) For growing food crops, for example wheat — good crops grow in the fertile land of plains.
  • (3) For growing cotton for clothes — our clothes are made from cotton.

Key Points

  • Plains are flat pieces of land.
  • Plains are very useful for human life: we build on them and grow food and cotton in them.

mcqs.q: Plains are ______ pieces of land.
mcqs.why: Big flat pieces of land are called plains. Buildings and crops are easy to grow in plain areas.

mcqs.q: Buildings are made easily in ______.
mcqs.why: Houses, schools, hospitals and offices are built in plains because buildings are made easily in plain areas.

mcqs.q: Good crops grow in the ______ land of plains.
mcqs.why: Good crops grow in the fertile land of plains, for example wheat and other food crops.

mcqs.q: Which food crop is named in this lesson as grown in plains?
mcqs.why: Wheat is the food crop named in this lesson; good crops like wheat grow in the fertile land of plains.

mcqs.q: Our clothes are made from ______ grown in plains.
mcqs.why: Cotton for clothes is grown in plains, and our clothes are made from cotton.

mcqs.q: Schools and hospitals are built in plains because ______.
mcqs.why: Buildings are made easily in plain areas, so houses, schools, hospitals and offices are built in plains.

mcqs.q: People live in plains in ______.
mcqs.why: One use of plains is building houses to live in, along with schools, hospitals and offices.

mcqs.q: Plains are very ______ for human life.
mcqs.why: Plains are very useful for human life because we build on them and grow food and cotton in them.

mcqs.q: Which of these is built in plains?
mcqs.why: Hospitals are among the buildings made in plains, together with houses, schools and offices.

mcqs.q: Plains give us land for ______.
mcqs.why: Plains are used for building houses, growing food crops and growing cotton for clothes.

lessons.title: Mountains
lessons.notes_html:
This lesson has no printed activity for students; these notes and questions are made from the lesson’s own text.

What Mountains Give Us

  • (1) Fresh and sweet water — snow falls on mountains; it melts and makes rivers and springs, from which we get drinking water.
  • The book says: we find springs of water in the mountains; these springs make rivers and lakes.
  • (2) Minerals — many mineral things are found in mountains, for example gold, silver and iron.
  • (3) Cool and clean air and beautiful scenery.

Key Points

  • Mountains are also a big natural resource for us.
  • They give us water, minerals, cool air and beautiful scenery.

mcqs.q: Springs of water are found in ______.
mcqs.why: The book says: we find springs of water in the mountains; these springs make rivers and lakes.

mcqs.q: Springs in the mountains make ______.
mcqs.why: The springs of water in the mountains make rivers and lakes, from which we get water.

mcqs.q: Snow falls on mountains and ______ to make rivers.
mcqs.why: Snow falls on mountains; it melts and makes rivers and springs from which we get drinking water.

mcqs.q: From mountain rivers and springs we get ______.
mcqs.why: Mountains give us fresh and sweet water; the melted snow makes rivers and springs of drinking water.

mcqs.q: Which of these minerals is found in mountains?
mcqs.why: Many mineral things are found in mountains, for example gold, silver and iron.

mcqs.q: Iron is a ______ found in mountains.
mcqs.why: Gold, silver and iron are minerals, and many minerals are found in mountains.

mcqs.why: Mountains give us cool and clean air and beautiful scenery, besides water and minerals.

mcqs.why: Mountains give us cool and clean air and beautiful scenery, so they are a big natural resource.

mcqs.q: Mountains give us water, minerals and ______.
mcqs.why: Mountains give us fresh water, minerals like gold and iron, and cool and clean air.

mcqs.q: Mountains are a big ______ for us.
mcqs.why: Mountains are also a big natural resource for us, giving water, minerals and clean air.

lessons.title: Forests
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Forest?

  • A forest is a place where many trees grow close to each other and many things live there.

Why Forests Are Important

  • They are the home of many animals.
  • They keep the air clean and fresh.
  • Their wood is used in many things, for example desks, classroom doors and windows.
  • Some wood is also used as fuel for cooking.

If We Cut Down the Forests

  • The homes of animals will be destroyed.
  • The air will become dirty.
  • Wood will not be available.
  • The danger of floods in rains will increase.

Key Points

  • Forests are the home of animals and keep our air clean.
  • Cutting forests harms animals, air and people.

mcqs.q: A forest is a place where ______.
options: Many trees grow close to each other
mcqs.why: A forest is a place where many trees grow close to each other and many things live there.

mcqs.q: Forests are the home of ______.
mcqs.why: Forests are important because they are the home of many animals.

mcqs.q: Forests keep the air ______.
mcqs.why: Forests keep the air clean and fresh, which is one reason they are important for us.

mcqs.q: Wood from forests is used to make ______.
mcqs.why: Forest wood is used in many things, for example desks, classroom doors and windows.

mcqs.q: Some wood from forests is used as ______.
mcqs.why: Some wood is also used as fuel for cooking, besides making desks, doors and windows.

mcqs.q: If we cut down the forests, animals will ______.
mcqs.why: If we cut down the forests, the homes of animals will be destroyed.

mcqs.q: Cutting forests makes the air ______.
mcqs.why: Forests keep the air clean; if we cut them down, the air will become dirty.

mcqs.q: If forests are cut, the danger of ______ increases in rains.
mcqs.why: If we cut down the forests, the danger of floods in rains will increase.

mcqs.q: Many living things live in a ______.
mcqs.why: A forest is a place where many trees grow close to each other and many things live there.

mcqs.q: Forests are ______ for us.
mcqs.why: Forests are important: they are the home of animals, keep the air clean, and give us wood.

lessons.title: Problems of the Earth and Their Solutions
lessons.notes_html:
Activities That Harm the Land

  • (1) Throwing garbage and dirt — it makes the land dirty.
  • (2) Growing crops on the same land year after year without proper care — it makes the land weak.
  • (3) Cutting forests and digging the land for minerals — it destroys the homes of animals and spoils the environment.

Ways to Reduce the Problems

  • (1) Use things less, and reuse them — cloth, paper, wood, bottles and paper can be used again.
  • (2) Farmers should protect their land and fields.
  • (3) Make laws to protect forests and plant more trees.

Key Points

  • Garbage, careless farming and cutting forests harm the land.
  • Using less, reusing things and planting trees reduce the problems of the land.

mcqs.q: Throwing garbage and dirt makes the land ______.
mcqs.why: Throwing garbage and dirt is a human activity that affects the land; it makes the land dirty.

mcqs.q: Growing crops on the same land year after year without care makes the land ______.
mcqs.why: Growing crops on the same land year after year without proper care makes the land weak.

mcqs.q: Cutting forests destroys the homes of ______.
mcqs.why: Cutting forests and digging the land for minerals destroys the homes of animals and spoils the environment.

mcqs.q: Digging the land for minerals spoils the ______.
mcqs.why: Cutting forests and digging for minerals spoils the environment, so we should reduce such activities.

mcqs.q: To reduce land problems, we should use things ______.
mcqs.why: We can reduce the problems by using things less and reusing them, like cloth, paper, wood and bottles.

mcqs.q: Which of these can we reuse?
mcqs.why: We can reuse bottles and paper, and also cloth and wood, instead of throwing them away.

mcqs.q: Farmers should ______ their land and fields.
mcqs.why: Farmers should protect their land and fields so that the land does not become weak.

mcqs.q: Laws should be made to protect ______.
mcqs.why: Making laws to protect forests is one way to reduce the problems of the land.

mcqs.q: We should plant ______ trees.
mcqs.why: Planting more trees helps protect forests and reduces the problems of the land.

mcqs.q: Reusing a bottle means ______.
options: Using it again instead of throwing it away
mcqs.why: Reuse means using things like bottles and paper again, which reduces the problems of the land.

lessons.title: End of Unit 6 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Words about the Land

  • We breathe in air; we eat the food grown in the land; all living things need air, food and water to live.
  • We build our houses in the plain. Pieces of land a little higher than the surface are called hills and mountains.
  • Gold, marble and silver are examples of minerals.
  • Big flat pieces of land are called plains; land where a large number of trees grow close to each other is called a forest.

Minerals in Daily Life

  • Jewellery is made from precious minerals like gold and silver.
  • The mausoleum of Quaid-e-Azam is built from white marble.
  • Rods are made from strong iron. Three things made from iron are a knife, a frying pan (karahi) and a door lock.
  • Mineral products we use: iron, salt and natural gas.

Jobs and Natural Resources

  • A student uses wood and paper; a farmer uses land, water and seeds; a fisherman uses water and fish; a housewife uses water, vegetables and fuel; a jeweller uses gold and silver; a zoo worker uses fodder and water; a carpenter uses wood.

Land Problems in Our Area

  • People throw garbage on roads and in empty plots; cutting of trees has decreased greenery and increased the danger of floods; growing crops continuously on the same land is making it weak.
  • Solutions: put garbage in the dustbin, plant more trees and take care of the land.

Key Points

  • Natural resources are surely used in every work.
  • Minerals are found in the land and are very useful in daily life.

mcqs.q: Big flat pieces of land are called ______.

mcqs.q: Land where many trees grow close to each other is called a ______.
mcqs.why: Such land on which a large number of trees grow close to each other is called a forest.

options: Precious minerals like gold and silver
mcqs.why: Jewellery is made from precious minerals like gold and silver, which are found in the land.

mcqs.q: The mausoleum of Quaid-e-Azam is built from ______.
mcqs.why: The mausoleum of Quaid-e-Azam is built from white marble, which is a mineral from the land.

mcqs.q: Rods are made from strong ______.
mcqs.why: Rods are made from strong iron. A knife, a frying pan and a door lock are also made from iron.

mcqs.q: A carpenter uses ______ in his work.
mcqs.why: A carpenter uses wood in his work; a jeweller uses gold and silver, and a fisherman uses water and fish.

mcqs.q: A jeweller uses ______ in his work.
mcqs.why: A jeweller uses minerals like gold and silver in his work of making jewellery.

mcqs.q: To solve the land problems of our area, we should put garbage in the ______.
mcqs.why: We should put garbage in the dustbin, plant more trees and take care of the land.

lessons.title: Water
lessons.notes_html:
Water on the Earth

  • The surface of the earth is covered with land and water.
  • About three-fourths (3/4) of the surface of the earth is covered with water.

Salty and Fresh Water

  • Salty water is found in oceans and seas.
  • Fresh (sweet) water is found in rivers, lakes, springs, streams, under the ground and from rain.
  • Most of the water on earth is not fit for drinking because it is salty; drinking salty water spoils health.

Sources of Water in the Picture

  • A pond or lake, a well (water taken out with a bucket), a waterfall and stream flowing down from the mountains, a canal or river, and the sea — the biggest store of salty water.

Key Points

  • Most of the earth is covered with water, but most of it is salty.
  • We drink fresh water from rivers, lakes, springs, wells and rain.

mcqs.q: The surface of the earth is covered with ______.
mcqs.why: The surface of the earth is covered with land and water, and most of it is water.

mcqs.q: About how much of the earth’s surface is covered with water?
mcqs.why: About three-fourths (3/4) part of the surface of the earth is covered with water.

mcqs.q: Salty water is found in ______.
mcqs.why: Salty water is found in oceans and seas. Fresh water is found in rivers, lakes and springs.

mcqs.q: Fresh (sweet) water is found in ______.
mcqs.why: Fresh (sweet) water is found in rivers, lakes, springs, streams, under the ground and from rain.

mcqs.q: Rain gives us ______ water.
mcqs.why: Rain is one of the sources of fresh (sweet) water, along with rivers, lakes and springs.

mcqs.q: Most of the earth’s water is not fit for drinking because it is ______.
mcqs.why: Most of the water found on the surface of the earth is not fit for drinking because it is salty.

mcqs.q: Drinking salty water ______.
mcqs.why: Drinking salty water spoils health, so we should drink only fresh water.

mcqs.q: The biggest store of salty water is the ______.
mcqs.why: The sea is the biggest store of salty water among the sources shown in the picture.

mcqs.q: Water is taken out with a bucket from a ______.
mcqs.why: A well is the source from where water is taken out with a bucket.

mcqs.q: Water flowing down from the mountains is a ______.
mcqs.why: A waterfall and stream is water flowing down from the mountains, as labelled in the picture.

lessons.title: How Water Reaches Our Homes
lessons.notes_html:
The Journey of Water

  • Mountain — the snow melts — it flows in a river — it is stored in a water reservoir, where the water is cleaned — then it reaches the tap of our homes.
  • Water also comes into wells from under the ground.

Clean Water to Drink

  • We should drink water from the glass that is clean and clear.
  • Drinking cloudy (muddy) water can cause diseases; clean water is good for health.
  • At home we should drink water after filtering or boiling it.

Key Points

  • Water travels from the mountains to our taps through rivers and reservoirs.
  • Always drink clean water; filter or boil it at home.

mcqs.q: The water in our taps comes from the mountains through a ______.
mcqs.why: Snow melts on the mountains, flows in a river, is cleaned in a reservoir, and then reaches the tap of our homes.

mcqs.q: On the mountains, ______ melts to become water.
mcqs.why: With the heat of the sun, the snow on the mountains melts and becomes water.

mcqs.q: River water is stored in a ______, where it is cleaned.
mcqs.why: River water is stored in a water reservoir where the water is cleaned, before it comes to our taps.

mcqs.q: Water is cleaned in the reservoir before it reaches our ______.
mcqs.why: The journey of water ends at the tap of our homes, after it is cleaned in the reservoir.

mcqs.q: We should drink water from the glass that is ______.
mcqs.why: I will drink water from the glass which has clean and clear water, because clean water is good for health.

mcqs.q: Drinking cloudy (muddy) water can cause ______.
mcqs.why: Drinking cloudy water can cause diseases, while clean water is good for health.

mcqs.q: At home, we should drink water after ______.
mcqs.why: At home we should drink water after filtering or boiling it, so that it stays clean and safe.

mcqs.q: The water in wells comes from ______.
mcqs.why: Water comes into wells from under the ground; people also bring underground water through tube wells and hand pumps.

mcqs.q: The journey of water in this lesson ends at ______.
mcqs.why: The flow chart shows: mountain, snow melts, river, reservoir, and at the end the tap of our homes.

mcqs.why: Clean water is good for health, while cloudy water can cause diseases.

lessons.title: Importance of Water

  • Brushing teeth — 2 times; taking a bath — 1 time; drinking — 6 to 8 times; cooking — 3 times; washing dishes — 3 times; watering plants — 1 time; washing clothes — 1 time.

Least and Most

  • The least water is used for brushing teeth and watering plants.
  • The most water is used for taking a bath and washing clothes.

Key Points

  • Water is very important for daily life.
  • We use water many times every day for drinking, cooking, washing and bathing.

lessons.title: Use Water Carefully
lessons.notes_html:
This lesson has no separate activity box; these notes and questions are made from the list of ways of saving water told in the lesson.

Six Ways to Save Water

  • (1) Keep the tap closed while brushing teeth.
  • (2) Take a bath in less time — take a short bath.
  • (3) For cleaning the house, use a bucket and mug instead of a pipe.
  • (4) Do not let water keep running while washing dishes.
  • (5) Get leaking pipes and taps repaired so that water stops leaking.
  • (6) Teach others also to save water.

Key Points

  • Water is a precious blessing; it should not be wasted.
  • Saving water is easy if we are careful every day.

lessons.title: End of Unit 7 Exercise (Questions 1 to 3)
lessons.notes_html:
From Snow to River

  • On a big mountain there is white snow on its top. With the heat of the sun, the snow melts and becomes water.
  • That water flows down as a small stream and then becomes a big river and flows towards the plains. We use river water for drinking, farming and other works.

Questions and Answers

  • The biggest part of the surface of the earth is covered with water.
  • Fresh water is found in rivers, lakes and springs (underground water and rain also give fresh water).
  • People bring underground water to their homes by digging wells, or by tube wells and hand pumps.
  • Three living things which need water to live: human beings, animals and plants.

How Water Is Used

  • Animals: drink water and bathe in it; some animals live in water itself, for example fish.
  • My family: we drink water and use it for cooking, washing dishes and clothes and taking a bath.
  • Farmers: water their crops and fields and give water to animals.
  • Plants: grow with water and make their food; without water plants dry up.

Key Points

  • All living things need water to live.
  • Animals, people, farmers and plants all use water in different ways.

mcqs.q: Farmers use water for ______.

mcqs.q: Without water, plants ______.
mcqs.why: Plants grow with water and make their food; without water plants dry up.

mcqs.q: My family uses water for cooking and ______.

mcqs.why: We use the river's water for drinking, farming and other works, as the exercise tells us.

lessons.title: Sources of Water and Saving Water
lessons.notes_html:
Sources of Water in the Pictures

  • (1) A river — a boat is on it. (2) A glacier in the mountains. (3) The sea. (4) A lake between mountains. (5) A well.
  • We get water from rivers, lakes, wells and rain.

How People Waste Water — and What to Do Instead

  • Washing a car with a pipe wastes water — wash it with a bucket and a cloth instead.
  • Leaving the tap open while brushing teeth or washing hands — open the tap only when needed.
  • Water flowing from broken taps and pipes — get them fixed at once.
  • Washing the street and courtyard with a pipe — clean with a broom instead.
  • Keeping the tap open under the pots — turn off the tap after filling the pots.

Key Points

  • Rivers, glaciers, seas, lakes and wells are sources of water.
  • We should stop every way of wasting water.

mcqs.q: A big piece of ice in the mountains is called a ______.
mcqs.why: In the pictures of water sources, the glacier in the mountains is one of the sources of water.

mcqs.why: Wash the car with a bucket and a cloth instead of a pipe to save water.

mcqs.why: Water keeps flowing from broken taps and pipes; instead they should be fixed at once.

mcqs.why: Washing the street with a pipe wastes water; instead we should clean it with a broom.

mcqs.why: Keeping the tap open under the pots wastes water; we should turn off the tap after filling the pots.

mcqs.q: We get water from rivers, lakes, wells and ______.
mcqs.why: We get water from rivers, lakes, wells and rain, as this exercise tells us.

mcqs.q: The sea is a source of ______ water.
mcqs.why: The sea is one of the sources of water shown in the pictures, and its water is salty.

mcqs.q: Leaving the tap open while brushing teeth ______.
mcqs.why: People waste water by leaving the tap open while brushing teeth; they should open the tap only when needed.

chapters.title: Plants and their Parts and Functions

lessons.title: Plants Around Us
lessons.notes_html:
Plants Around Me

  • Three plants around me are: (i) a neem tree, (ii) a rose plant, (iii) a sunflower plant.
  • Plants are one of the many beautiful gifts of nature and they are very useful for us.

Plants in the Pictures

  • (1) A big green tree — a neem tree. (2) A date palm tree. (3) A flowering plant in a pot with red flowers — hibiscus (China rose). (4) Sunflowers.

Key Points

  • We eat some plants, and we use some plants to make other things.
  • Plants around us are beautiful and useful gifts of nature.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a plant around us?
mcqs.why: Three plants around me are a neem tree, a rose plant and a sunflower plant.

mcqs.q: A date palm is a ______.
mcqs.why: In the pictures, the date palm tree is one of the plants named in this lesson.

mcqs.q: The flowering plant in a pot with red flowers is ______.
mcqs.why: The flowering plant in a pot with red flowers is hibiscus, also called China rose.

mcqs.why: The sunflower plant is one of the plants around us named in this lesson.

mcqs.why: We eat some plants and we use some plants to make other things.

mcqs.why: We eat some plants, and we use some plants to make other things.

mcqs.why: Plants are one of the many beautiful gifts of nature and they are very useful for us.

mcqs.why: A rose plant is one of the plants around us, and it is a flowering plant.

mcqs.why: Sunflowers are the plants with big yellow flowers shown in the pictures of this lesson.

mcqs.why: Plants are very useful for us; we eat some of them and make other things from some of them.

lessons.title: Parts of Plants and Their Functions
lessons.notes_html:
Parts of a Plant

  • The flower is at the top, the leaves are below it, the stem and its branches are in the middle, and the roots are under the ground.

Roots

  • Roots grow down into the soil and have many small branches; there is dirt on them because they grow underground in the soil.
  • Roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil, keep the plant fixed firmly, and give support to the plant to stand straight.
  • We eat some roots as food, such as carrot, radish and arvi — these roots store food in them.
  • In the cotton-strip experiment, water slowly moved up the strip — in the same way roots absorb water and it travels through the whole plant.

Stem and Leaves

  • The stem keeps the plant standing straight, supports the branches, leaves, flowers and fruits, and takes water from the roots to the leaves. Some plants store food in their stems, such as sugarcane.
  • In the lettuce experiment, the stem carried the coloured water up, and the leaf changed its colour.
  • Leaves are of three types: simple leaves, compound leaves and needle leaves (like the pine).

Flowers

  • Flowers are brightly coloured so that they attract butterflies and bees; the bees drink nectar and carry pollen, which helps in pollination.
  • Flowers make the fruits that we eat; seeds are in the fruit, and new plants grow from the seeds: guava flower — guava fruit — seeds — new guava plant.

Key Points

  • Roots absorb water, the stem carries it up, leaves make food, and flowers make fruits and seeds.
  • Every part of the plant helps the plant in some way.

mcqs.q: The parts of a plant are flower, leaves, stem and ______.
mcqs.why: The parts of a plant are: the flower at the top, the leaves, the stem and its branches, and the roots under the ground.

mcqs.q: Roots grow ______.
options: Under the ground, into the soil
mcqs.why: Roots grow underground into the soil, and they have many small branches spread out in every direction.

mcqs.q: Roots absorb ______ from the soil.
mcqs.why: Roots suck up water and nutrients from the soil; that is why there is dirt on the roots.

mcqs.q: Roots have small branches so that they can ______.
options: Absorb more water and hold the plant firmly
mcqs.why: Roots have small branches so that they can spread out and absorb more water and nutrients, and hold the plant firmly.

mcqs.q: We eat some roots as food, such as ______.
mcqs.why: Three roots that we eat are carrot, radish and arvi. These roots store food in them.

mcqs.why: Roots give support to the plant to stand straight, and they also absorb water and nutrients.

mcqs.why: The stem takes water from the roots and gives it to the leaves; in the lettuce experiment it carried coloured water up.

mcqs.q: Sugarcane stores food in its ______.
mcqs.why: Some plants also store food in their stems, such as sugarcane.

mcqs.q: Flowers are brightly coloured to ______.
mcqs.why: Flowers are brightly colored so that they can attract butterflies and bees to the plants, which help in pollination.

mcqs.q: Bees and butterflies help the plant in ______.
mcqs.why: Bees and butterflies drink the nectar and carry pollen from flower to flower, which helps in pollination.

lessons.title: End of Unit 8 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
What a Plant Needs

  • A plant needs four things to grow: (i) water, (ii) sunlight, (iii) air, (iv) soil and its nutrients.
  • Roots take in water from the soil; the stem of a tree is called the trunk; the colourful part of a plant is the flower; leaves make food for the plant; flowers make fruit.

Rose Plant and Date Palm

  • Similar: both are green; both have roots, a stem and leaves; both are flowering plants; both need water, sunlight and air to grow.
  • Different: the rose is a small plant and the date palm is a very tall tree; the rose stem is thin and has thorns, the palm trunk is thick and straight; the rose has pink flowers, the date palm bears dates as its fruit.

Vegetables and Plant Parts

  • Spinach/lettuce — leaf; maize (corn) — fruit (seeds); onion — stem (bulb); beans — fruit (pod); broccoli — flower; tomato — fruit; garlic — stem (bulb); cucumber — fruit; red capsicum — fruit.
  • Flowering or not: a pine tree is non-flowering; roses, a fruit tree and big flowers are flowering; a leafy bush is non-flowering.

Key Points

  • Plants that produce flowers and seeds are called flowering plants.
  • We eat different parts of different plants.

mcqs.q: A plant needs water, sunlight, air and ______ to grow.
mcqs.why: A plant needs four things to grow: water, sunlight, air, and soil with its nutrients.

mcqs.q: Roots take in ______ from the soil.
mcqs.why: Roots take in water from the soil, as the fill-in-the-blank exercise of this unit says.

mcqs.why: The stem of a tree is called the trunk. The trunk is the thick and strong part of the tree.

mcqs.why: The colourful part of a plant is the flower, and the fruit is also made from the flower.

mcqs.why: Flowers make fruit, and new plants grow from the seeds in the fruit, such as mangoes and oranges.

mcqs.why: The stem of the rose is thin and has thorns, whereas the trunk of the date palm is thick and straight.

mcqs.why: The date palm bears dates as its fruit, while the rose has pink and beautiful flowers.

mcqs.q: Broccoli is the ______ part of its plant.
mcqs.why: In the vegetable pictures, broccoli is the flower part of its plant, and spinach is a leaf.

mcqs.q: A pine tree is a ______ plant.
mcqs.why: A pine tree with needle leaves is a non-flowering plant; roses and fruit trees are flowering plants.

lessons.title: Animals Around Us
lessons.notes_html:
This is an activity lesson: you name five animals that live around you.

Five Animals Around Me

  • (1) Dog — lives in the home and street.
  • (2) Cat — lives in homes.
  • (3) Pigeon — lives on roofs and trees.
  • (4) Goat — is kept in villages and homes.

  • We should behave with animals with love.

mcqs.q: A dog lives in ______.

mcqs.q: A pigeon lives on ______.
mcqs.why: A pigeon lives on roofs and trees, as this lesson tells us about animals around us.

mcqs.q: A goat is kept in ______.
mcqs.why: A goat is kept in villages and homes. It is one of the five animals named in this lesson.

mcqs.q: A sparrow lives ______.
mcqs.why: The sparrow, or house sparrow, lives near homes.

mcqs.q: A cat lives in ______.
mcqs.why: A cat lives in homes. It is one of the animals that live around us.

mcqs.q: Animals around us are a part of our ______.
mcqs.why: These animals are a part of our environment, and we should behave with them with love.

mcqs.q: We should behave with animals with ______.
mcqs.why: Animals around us are part of our environment, so we should behave with them with love.

lessons.title: Places Where Animals Live
lessons.notes_html:
Where Animals Live

  • Fish — in the water (in the lake). Parrot — on the tree. Frog — at the edge of the water and in the grass. Duck — in the water (it swims). Monkey — on the tree. Snake — in the grass and in a burrow. Deer — in the grass and forest.
  • Every animal lives at such a place where it gets food and safety.

Groups of Animals

  • With four legs: cow, horse, dog. With wings: pigeon, parrot, butterfly. Crawling animals: snake, earthworm, lizard. With a shell: tortoise, snail.

Body Parts and Their Work

  • A bird flies with its wings. A duck swims with its webbed feet. A horse runs and walks with its legs. An insect flies with its wings.
  • Every animal’s body parts are made for its special work.

Key Points

  • Animals live where they get food and safety.
  • The body structures of animals help them in living and moving.

mcqs.q: A fish lives ______.
mcqs.why: A fish lives in the water, in the lake, as the picture activity of this lesson shows.

mcqs.why: A frog lives at the edge of the water and in the grass.

mcqs.why: A snake lives in the grass and in a burrow, and it is a crawling animal.

mcqs.why: A horse runs and walks with its legs. Every animal's body parts are made for its special work.

lessons.title: Homes of Animals
lessons.notes_html:
The Story of Chhota Bani

  • Babbar Sher Leo (the lion) had invited all the animals of the jungle to his birthday party. He could not invite Fish Fini only, because she cannot live without water.
  • Bani’s parents went first to the anthill. A lion lives in a den. The monkey lived in a tree.
  • They found Bani near the river. Bani had gone towards the river to invite Fish Fini to the party, so that she too could join happily.

Animals and Their Homes

  • Rabbit — burrow (a hole-home made in the ground). Ant — anthill. Bird — nest made on a tree. Fish — pond/water. Cow — cattle pen (enclosed field).
  • Lions and tigers live in dens; a honeybee’s home is a hive; a spider’s home is a web; monkeys and insects live on trees.

Key Points

  • Every animal has its own home where it lives safely.

mcqs.q: Who invited all the animals to his birthday party?
mcqs.why: Babbar Sher Leo (the lion) had invited all the animals of the jungle to his birthday party.

mcqs.why: Leo could not invite Fish Fini only, because she cannot live without water.

lessons.title: Animals and Their Babies
lessons.notes_html:
How Birds Raise Their Babies

  • (1) Birds make nests. (2) The female lays eggs in the nest. (3) The parent birds sit on them. (4) The eggs hatch and the chicks come out. (5) The parent birds feed grain to the chicks.

How Mothers Help Their Babies

  • A hen teaches her chicks to peck grain. A lioness carries her cub in her mouth. An elephant bathes her calf by spraying water. A cat shows love to her kitten. A kangaroo protects her baby in her pouch. A bird feeds her chicks.
  • The poem tells us that every mother loves her babies: she keeps them calm and warm, brings food and water, protects them from danger, and cleans them.

Babies and Their Names

  • Sheep — lamb; cat — kitten; dog — puppy; hen — chick; cow — calf; swan — cygnet; frog — tadpole; horse — foal; butterfly — caterpillar; duck — duckling; lion — cub.
  • Babies that do not look like their parents: the frog’s tadpole and the butterfly’s caterpillar — they change their shape when they grow up. Babies that look like their parents: kitten and calf.

Key Points

  • Every animal’s baby has its own special name.
  • Every mother loves her babies and protects them.

mcqs.why: A bird's babies are called chicks. The eggs hatch and the chicks come out of them.

mcqs.why: A dog's baby is a puppy. A cat's baby is a kitten and a hen's baby is a chick.

mcqs.q: The baby of a horse is a ______.
mcqs.why: A horse's baby is a foal. It looks like its parents from birth.

mcqs.q: The baby of a frog is a ______.
mcqs.why: A frog's baby is a tadpole. It does not look like its parents and changes its shape when it grows up.

mcqs.q: The baby of a butterfly is a ______.
mcqs.why: A butterfly's baby is a caterpillar, which changes its shape when it grows up.

lessons.title: End of Unit 9 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Homes Again

  • A rabbit’s burrow is a hole in the ground with small rooms inside; the rabbit lives in it and hides in it at the time of danger.
  • A spider’s web is a round web in the branches of a tree or in a corner; the spider lives in it and traps insects in it and eats them.
  • Birds live in nests, monkeys live in trees, rabbits live in burrows and cows live in cattle pens.

How Body Structures Help

  • The camel’s hump — food (fat) is stored in it, so the camel can stay without food for many days in the desert.
  • The lion’s sharp teeth — help in chewing food, eating meat and hunting. The fish’s fins — help in swimming. The duck’s webbed feet — help in swimming.
  • The bird’s beak — helps in eating food and pecking grain. The elephant’s trunk — helps in reaching leaves for food and in lifting things. The tortoise’s shell — is for protection; at the time of danger the tortoise hides in it.

The Different One

  • Cat, cow, dog, hen — the hen is different: the others are mammals; the hen is a bird. Crow, horse, parrot, peacock — the horse is different: the others can fly. Tortoise, fish, lizard, snake — the fish is different: the others are reptiles. Butterfly, dolphin, starfish, whale — the butterfly is different: the others are sea animals. Crocodile, frog, monkey, green turtle — the monkey is different: the others live in or near water.

How Animals Move and Help Us

  • Cow — walks; lion — runs; horse — runs; fish — swims; parrot — flies; earthworm — crawls; kangaroo — hops; crow — flies.
  • Cow gives us milk; goat gives milk and meat; hen gives eggs and meat; dog guards the house; horse helps in riding and carrying loads.

Key Points

  • Every animal makes its home for its safety.
  • Animals are very useful for us, so we should take care of them.

mcqs.q: The camel’s hump stores ______.

mcqs.why: The camel's hump stores food, so the camel can stay without food for many days in the desert.

mcqs.why: The hen is different because the other three are mammals; the hen is a bird: it has two legs, wings, and it lays eggs.

mcqs.why: An earthworm crawls. Crawling animals move along the ground, like the snake and the lizard.

mcqs.why: A dog guards the house. A cow gives us milk and a hen gives eggs and meat.

lessons.title: Using the Earth’s Resources to Meet Our Needs

lessons.title: Farming
lessons.notes_html:
Main Crops of Pakistan

  • The five main big crops of Pakistan are: (1) wheat, (2) rice, (3) cotton, (4) sugarcane, (5) maize (corn).

Where Our Products Come From

  • Biscuits are made from wheat flour. Jewellery is made from gold. Toffee is made from sugar, which comes from sugarcane. Corn oil is made from maize. Furniture is made from the wood of trees.

Animals Reared in Sindh

  • Animals reared in Sindh are sheep and goats, cows and buffaloes, and hens.
  • From hens we get eggs and meat. From cows, buffaloes, goats and sheep we get milk.
  • From milk, butter, lassi, yoghurt and cheese are made, and sweets are also made from milk.
  • From the skins of animals, leather is made, from which shoes, jackets and bags are made.
  • Rearing animals is a big source of income for farmers.

Key Points

  • Our daily things are made from natural sources only.
  • Farmers grow crops and rear animals with great hard work.

mcqs.why: Leather is made from animals' skins, and shoes, jackets and bags are made from leather.

mcqs.why: The animals whose milk we drink are the cow, the buffalo and the goat.

mcqs.why: Rearing animals is a big source of income for farmers, besides growing crops.

lessons.title: Materials and Tools Used in Construction
lessons.notes_html:
Natural and Man-Made Materials

  • Metals are strong, hard and shiny. Clay is soft and can be moulded easily. Wood is a natural thing. Steel is a strong but light material.
  • Plastic is not a natural thing; it is man-made. Pipes are made from plastic, not from glass.
  • Natural things: clay, wood, sand, gravel, leaves and twigs. Man-made things: glass, cement, concrete, steel, plastic.

Tools and Their Users

  • Pipe wrench — a plumber (for fitting and repairing pipes). Hammer — a carpenter (for hammering nails). Trowel — a mason (for applying mortar). Paint brush — a painter (for painting walls).

Properties of Materials

Famous Buildings

  • Taj Mahal — Agra, India. Shahjahani Mosque — Thatta, Sindh. Quaid-e-Azam International Airport — Karachi. Burj Al Arab — Dubai. HBL Plaza — Karachi. Eiffel Tower — Paris, France.

Key Points

  • Building materials can be divided into natural and man-made things.
  • Every craftsman has his own tools.
