lessons.title: Heat
lessons.notes_html:
The Sun Is the Source of Heat

  • In the sunlight we feel heat (warmth); in the classroom we feel cool, because the sun is the real source of heat and where sunlight falls directly, there is more heat.

The Towel Experiment

  • A wet towel kept in the sunlight dries first, because the heat of the sun quickly turns water into vapour.
  • Heat made the drying faster; the towel’s water became vapour and went into the air.

Sources of Heat and Their Uses

  • Wood stove — wood; gas heater — gas; coal iron — coal; wood fire — wood.
  • A pot on a gas stove — gas, for cooking food. A BBQ grill — coal, for roasting food. People around a fire at night — wood, for keeping warm. A car — petrol, for running the car. Clothes in the sun — the sun, for drying clothes. An electric iron — electricity, for pressing clothes.

The Ice Race

  • The group won which rubbed the ice bag fast between their hands and kept it in the sun’s heat.
  • Methods to melt ice: rubbing between hands, holding in warm hands, keeping in the sunlight, keeping near warm air or warm water. With heat, ice changes into water.

Key Points

  • The sun is the real source of heat.
  • Heat dries wet things, cooks food, keeps us warm and melts ice.

lessons.title: Light
lessons.notes_html:
We Need Light to See

  • In the daytime the source of light is the sun.
  • In a dark room we cannot see anything clearly. When a friend enters holding a burning candle, we can see the things, because light falls on the things and our eyes can see them.
  • Other man-made sources of light are: bulb, tube light, torch, lantern (oil lamp) and table lamp.

Near the Source, More Light and Heat

  • People sitting closer to the fire get more heat; the farther you are from the source, the less heat you get.
  • Children sitting near the tube light can read better, because more light falls on the book.

Natural and Man-Made Sources

  • Bulb — man-made; torch — man-made; sun — natural; burning match/fire — man-made; star — natural; oil lamp/lantern — man-made.
  • Some animals make their own light, for example the firefly.

Key Points

  • The sun is our natural source of light in the daytime.
  • At night we use man-made sources like a bulb and a torch.

lessons.notes_html:
Things That Give Light

  • Things which give light: fire, bulb, sun, torch, traffic light, lighthouse, table lamp, TV and star.
  • Things which do not give light: chair, desk and pencils — they are only seen in the light of others.

Seeing in Day and Night

  • We see things with our eyes.
  • In the day we can see easily, because the sun’s light falls on everything. At night light is less, so we need man-made light like a bulb and torch.

Only Light, Only Heat, or Both

  • Only light: TV, tube light, torch. Only heat: electric iron, electric heater. Both heat and light: sun, fire, candle/lamp.
  • The natural source in the list is the sun; the fire in the picture is lit by man, so it is also counted among the man-made.

lessons.title: Learning from the Lives and Teachings of the Prophets
lessons.notes_html:
Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)

  • Five noble qualities: Sadiq (always truthful), Amin (trustworthy), merciful, gentle, and forgiving.
  • He was born in Makkah Mukarramah in the year 571. Allah granted him prophethood at the age of 40 years.
  • The people of Makkah called him Sadiq and Amin because he always spoke the truth and was honest; people kept their trusts with him.
  • He taught: worship of one Allah alone, respect for parents, gentleness with elders, love with children, good behaviour with neighbours and helping the poor.
  • An old woman threw garbage on him daily; when one day no garbage came, he visited her, found her ill, and forgave her — on this kindness she felt ashamed and became a Muslim.
  • The book revealed to him is the Holy Quran, which is the last book.

Hazrat Musa (AS)

  • He was born in Egypt. In his time the rulers of Egypt were called Pharaoh.
  • The astrologers had told Pharaoh that a boy born in Bani Israel would end his kingdom, so Pharaoh began to get the boys killed. Musa’s mother put him in a box in the River Nile; Pharaoh’s wife Bibi Asiya raised him.
  • He took his people out of Egypt; at the Red Sea Allah made a path and Pharaoh’s army drowned. At Mount Sinai Allah spoke to him.
  • The book revealed to him is the Taurat, and his followers are called Jews. His qualities: bravery, opposing cruelty, and trust in Allah.

Hazrat Isa (AS)

  • He was born in Bethlehem. Allah gave him the power to show miracles: he cured the sick, gave sight to the blind and raised the dead by Allah’s command.
  • His qualities: kindness, forgiving, giving charity secretly, sharing, and being a great teacher.
  • The book revealed to him is the Injeel, and his followers are called Christians.

Key Points

  • We should learn truthfulness, honesty, kindness and forgiveness from the lives of the Prophets.

lessons.title: Being Just (Being Honest)
lessons.notes_html:
The Story of Faiza

  • Faiza’s three unfair works: at meal time she would take more food than her share; while talking she would not wait for her turn; in games she always wanted to come first and did not follow the rules.

How Faiza Became Fair

  • After her mother explained to her, Faiza began to take only her share, began to wait for her turn, and began to play according to the rules.
  • With this she herself began to feel good, and her brothers and sisters also began to like her.

What We Should Do

  • If my behaviour is not fair, I will say sorry and change my behaviour to become fair.
  • By apologising and changing behaviour, a person becomes better.

Key Points

  • Being just means taking only our share, waiting for our turn and following the rules.

lessons.notes_html:
The Story of Ali

  • Ali went to the bazaar with his father. He helped his father by carrying the shopping bags home.
  • He also picked up the things that had fallen from the bag of the man walking ahead and helped him.
  • Every person needs help.

Waiting for Your Turn

  • Waiting for your turn is very important, because it keeps order, nobody pushes, and everyone gets an equal chance.
  • A turn is necessary in food at home, in a queue at school, and in speaking in class.

Seema and Ayesha

  • Seema took Ayesha’s new toy car without asking and did not give Ayesha even one turn; Ayesha said they should play together.
  • When someone takes our things without asking, we feel hurt and angry.
  • Sharing means using your thing together with another person and being happy together.
  • When you need a thing that someone else has, politely ask for it and use it by turns.

Key Points

  • Helping others and waiting for our turn make everyone happy.

How Plants Are Useful

Fruits With and Without Seeds

The Leaf Experiment
